requiredFindings.title: The new Python repr formatter does not reproduce non-ASCII non-printable characters
requiredFindings.finding: python_repr escapes ASCII controls and DEL but emits every other character literally. Python repr also escapes non-printable Unicode. For a malformed internal root consisting of slash then U+0085, the bound reference returns a NATIVE_UNIT_ROOT_REPRESENTATION key whose value is quoted slash followed by literal backslash-x85; for slash then U+2028 it uses literal backslash-u2028. Candidate source emits the actual U+0085/U+2028 characters. Thus the newly claimed exact refusal keys differ, and all current malformed-root vectors miss this branch. Both inputs are rejected, so this is a refusal-reproduction defect rather than an admission bypass.
requiredFindings.requiredChange: Match the selected reference string representation for non-printable Unicode in grammar refusals, or use an explicitly selected equivalent refusal representation through the proper design route. Add reference-generated malformed-root vectors for U+0085 and U+2028, and verify exact key equality without changing accepted-root semantics.
